title: Jersey City AV Game

dims.risk: Backlash risk: chance a serious AV crash forces an MVC halt mid-pilot
dims.congestion: Traffic: added vehicle-miles from empty robotaxi trips (deadheading)

scale: Effects are in the points defined under 'units', relative to today, at full driverless operation (scaled by the law's driverless share). Ranges [lo, hi] drive the robustness runs.

stall.label: Stall (no AV law)
stall.basis: Status quo: NJ has no driverless framework; S1677 sits in Senate Budget & Appropriations, and its prior version (S4702) died.

s1677.label: S1677 as written
s1677.basis: 3-yr pilot, human-driver phase first, cameras + 2 other sensor types, manual controls. Waymo says it delays launch to about 2028, so only part of the window runs driverless. Tesla is excluded. Safety validation is high: the human-driver phase, the 3-sensor rule, and the MVC Chief Administrator's power to halt an operator immediately.

amended.label: Industry-amended
amended.basis: The changes Waymo, Tesla and Chamber of Progress asked for: no safety-driver phase, a sensor-neutral rule, school-zone limits eased. Safety validation is low: no human-driver phase, and the sensor rule drops to cameras-only.

moratorium.label: Moratorium
moratorium.basis: The anti-AV petition's ask: stop AV testing in NJ to protect driver jobs.

open.label: Open curb
open.basis: No pick-up/drop-off rules. Bike JC and Safe Streets JC worry about AVs stopping in bike lanes; SF's mayor complained of Waymos blocking lanes.

managed.label: Managed curb
managed.basis: DOI under Kaplan sets pick-up/drop-off zones, data sharing and curb fees as part of the Vision Zero quick-build program.

restrict.label: Restrict curb
restrict.basis: No AV pick-ups on commercial corridors. Cities cannot ban state-licensed vehicles, but can choke curb access.

waymo.label: Waymo
waymo.basis: Safety: 95% fewer serious-injury crashes (271M rider-only miles, Waymo June 2026) x an assumed 2-3% share of JC vehicle-miles = 1.9-2.9% fewer crashes, i.e. 0.38-0.57 pt. Jobs: an assumed 4-8% of JC rideshare trips captured.

tesla.label: Tesla
tesla.basis: No verified crash rate: 36 NHTSA incident reports, and crashes during remote-operator takeovers. Efficacy is assumed to range from -50% to +90% x a 2.5% share of vehicle-miles, i.e. -0.25 to +0.45 pt. That wide band feeds the risk dimension. Lower entry cost because the fleet is consumer cars.

operators.hazard_basis: Assumed. Waymo is low: 271M rider-only miles and about 95% fewer serious-injury crashes. Tesla is high: 36 NHTSA incident reports, every remote-operator takeover ended in a collision, and no verified crash rate.

via.label: Via + Waymo integration
via.basis: JC paid ~$7.7M/yr; the city puts 2025 cost at $15.80/trip and cut service on July 1, 2026 to close a ~$90M gap. Chandler, AZ fills peak trips with Waymo at a $2 fare. Assumed saving $1-3M/yr (0.5-1.5 pt), and most of the cut hours restored. Needs Waymo in the city and a curb that is not restricted.

weights_basis: Weights are assumptions inferred from each actor's stated priorities (sources in ../stakeholders.json): Vision Zero for DOI, Bike JC and Safe Streets JC; the $90M deficit for the Mayor; the safety-framed bill and Zwicker's 'pro New Jersey safety'; Sherrill's NJ Transit budget and jobs priorities. Power scores come from the power map. Movers weigh their own priorities and a power-weighted coalition of everyone else equally (coalition = 0.5). NY-region actors (round 2) enter as coalition members only. They have no vote in Trenton, so their influence runs through their power-map score: NYC DOT 'centers workers'; IDG and ATU killed Hochul's plan over jobs; Open Plans focuses on congestion; AAA polling shows safety fears; Chamber of Progress pushes innovation; blind advocates want access. Round 3: Uber weighs innovation and its human-driver network equally (its NJ bill keeps 85% of rideshare work human); Teamsters weigh jobs above all (human-operator mandates); AAI weighs innovation and safety (federal framework). These are coalition-only players.
risk_basis: P(halt) = sum over entering operators of hazard x driverless share x (1 - law validation), capped at 0.9. A halt mid-window wipes out about half the expected AV benefits and revenue. Precedent: California DMV suspended Cruise's driverless permits on Oct 24, 2023, three weeks after one pedestrian-dragging crash. S1677 gives MVC's Chief Administrator the same immediate-halt power.

units.safety: 1 pt = 5% fewer serious-injury crashes in JC
units.risk: 1 pt = 50% chance of a forced halt
units.jobs: 1 pt = 10% of JC rideshare trips kept by human drivers
units.access: 1 pt = restoring the Via evening + Saturday service cut on July 1, 2026
units.innovation: 1 pt = a full commercial robotaxi launch in the NJ market
units.congestion: 1 pt = 2% of JC vehicle-miles (negative = more traffic)

normalization: Each actor's utility is divided by its largest absolute value over all reachable outcomes. Influence in the coalition term then comes from power-map scores, not from whose units are bigger.
congestion_basis: Open Plans/Hunter (July 2026): Waymo drives 1.71 miles per passenger mile vs 1.49 for NYC ride-hail, about 15% more per trip. At an assumed 2-3% share of JC vehicle-miles that is +0.3-0.45% VMT, i.e. -0.15 to -0.22 pt. Pooled Via trips offset some of it.

launch.question: Will autonomous vehicles operate on Jersey City streets in 2027, whatever happens to S1677?
launch.basis: NJ has no AV statute, so nothing authorizes or bans driverless operation. S1677/A3968 sits in Senate Budget & Appropriations, and its 2024-25 version (S4702) died. Operators can choose to launch; the State can respond after the fact. Precedent: autonomous delivery robots (Avride since Feb 2025, Coco) already operate in JC under city pilots with no state law, and the State did not step in even after a robot injured a cyclist.

modes.test: Supervised testing/mapping with safety drivers (what Waymo does in JC today)

launch.test_basis: Testing earns no fares, but it builds readiness. Waymo has mapped JC, Hoboken and the Newark area with human drivers since 2025.

gap.label: Legal gap (no statute)
gap.basis: Without a statute, a halt rests on MVC registration powers. California revoked Uber's 16 self-driving registrations a week after its unpermitted 2016 SF launch, but NJ's authority to do the same is untested, so a halt may only partly stick.

s1677.label: S1677 enacted before 2027
s1677.basis: The statute requires 50,000 supervised NJ miles and 3 sensor types, so Tesla is out. MVC gets explicit immediate-halt power, and only part of 2027 can run driverless.

launch.p_bill_basis: Assumed 10-30%: S1677 has sat in Budget & Appropriations since May 11, 2026, and its predecessor died after clearing the same committee.
launch.halt_basis: Cost to an operator whose driverless launch is halted: reputation and sunk launch costs. Cruise lost its CA permits in Oct 2023 and later shut down robotaxi service.
launch.permissionless_basis: Cost of running commercial driverless service with no explicit state authorization. NJ's TNC Act (N.J.S.A. 39:5H-2) defines a ride-hail driver as a person using a personal vehicle, so driverless ride-hail fits no license category. Waymo is permission-first: 'until New Jersey does the same, we will not be able to bring the same service', and it stopped NYC testing when permits lapsed. Tesla moved fast under Texas' permissive law, but runs with safety drivers in California, so its cost is lower but not zero. Calibrated so that 2026 matches Waymo's observed choice (test, not driverless).
launch.readiness_basis: Share of a full-scale service an operator could actually run that year. 2026: Waymo was still mapping JC, Hoboken and Newark with human drivers. 2027: mapping matures, and Waymo opened Denver, San Diego and Tampa in Sept 2026, about a year after announcing them.
